newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN warning wipes six pct off shares.
newsitem.headline: GAN warning wipes six pct off shares.

text.p: Shares in French state-controlled insurer GAN slid more than six percent on Friday after it said the recent runup in its stock price was unjustified and repeated warnings it was headed into the red for 1996.
The announcement fuelled speculation GAN could require more than the 10 billion franc ($1.8 billion) capital injection it originally said it might need to pave the way for its privatisation.
Earlier this month, the daily Le Monde said Groupe des Assurances Nationales could need up to 20 billion francs.
GAN, which had a 965 million franc half-year loss, said in October it would have a full year loss and would need fresh state funds before its privatisation, which it hoped would happen this year.
On Friday, the insurer said initial results from an audit of its property portfolio bore out expectations its results would be hit by its exposure to France's weak property market.
"It was indicated...the audit may have a negative impact on its 1996 accounts and the first available signs confirm this to be the case," GAN said in a statement.

"I think they've taken the occasion to announce the audit will show the need for a big provision and that's probably going to result in a very large loss and they will have to ask for more capital," said one analyst.
GAN, 80-percent state-owned, said the recent rise in its share price was not "justified by its fundamentals".

The statement knocked GAN's shares down 6.29 percent to 123.6 francs. The shares, on a downward path since its property woes surfaced several years ago, had risen from a low of 99 francs in mid-January, fuelled by speculation GAN could be a bid target in the current consolidation in the insurance sector.

GAN, whose troubles stem mainly from its property financing arm UIC, confirmed it was in talks with the government to seek a solution. A company source said GAN was discussing an aid package but the amount was not determined. More was expected to be known after a board meeting before the end of February.

The property audit will help determine the size of the state injection it needs. The package will also hinge on the amount of money raised by sale of its retail banking arm CIC. An earlier attempt to privatise CIC was scrapped for lack of suitors.

Analysts said they had no idea how much state capital GAN would need. But one called Le Monde's 20 billion franc estimate excessive and believed the final sum would be nearer the 10 billion GAN was initially reported to be seeking. "The government doesn't have 20 billion francs for this," he said.
Analysts have said recently privatised French insurer AGF might eye GAN as a bid target following the takeover by insurer Axa of rival UAP late last year.
"It can still be a takeover target if they can get a good, clean GAN, with its property problems stripped out," said one.
A person close to AGF said this week it would "have to wait and see how big is GAN's loss and what the government will do."

Analysts were reluctant to estimate the size of GAN's 1996 loss, due to be announced at the end of April, saying it would depend on provisions. They said they expected the shares to remain volatile and described the stock as highly speculative. ($= 5.677 French Francs)
